review_outline.summary: Belief Tomography defines and operationalizes the first measured estimand for the gap between an autonomous agent's published charter and its behavior under adversarial probing. The paper pairs a 16-result theory stack (impossibility, deception-detection frontier, certification limits, disclosure economics) with 21 pre-registered experiments, an audited verdict channel, and two pre-registered field nulls on production frontier models and a live honeypot fleet. All load-bearing numbers were verified against the paper text and the underlying artifacts during this review.

strengths.text: Unusually complete preregistration discipline: 21 experiments registered before data, every deviation and halt dated, estimator pinned to a frozen commit.

The two field nulls are results, not absences: kill gates passed, the foil-family contrast shows the instrument recovers graded structure when beliefs exist, and the nulls bound the operational claim from both directions.

The disclosure-economics section (recon externality, deception release, no-free-lunch frontier) is a genuine privacy contribution for TOPS: published security measurements treated as sensitive data with a quantified trade-off.

Honest instrumentation: seeded audit calibration (adjudication channel dominates the lexical oracle), estimator- and seed-robustness, and a canary false-positive halt adjudicated with a live-extracted inventory.

weaknesses.text: Citation base skews to 2025-2026 arXiv preprints (a field-scarcity property, but a journal reviewer will probe maturity); all IDs verified and differentiation explicit — keep the collision-scan artifact current.

Deception-op engagement depth is bounded by the plane's shallow command layer (complex invocations fail; the detection persona flags the plane via /proc fakery) — the E3 null is instrumented-null; disclose prominently and frame /proc hardening as a deployment finding.
Privacy framing can be strengthened: one explicit bridge sentence in the introduction mapping published tomograms to sensitive-data disclosure would anchor the TOPS placement.
The field-null section should contrast the null with the foil family recovering graded structure, so the null reads as 'instrument bounded the phenomenon', not 'instrument found nothing'.

questions.text: Would the authors release the probe library and the canary allowlist publicly, given the gaming-gap results imply disclosure degrades the diagnostic?
How does the estimand behave for agents that learn continuously between measurements (T13 covers one-shot learning; the multi-round regime is open)?
